android-clipboard-history.title: How to see your clipboard history on Android
android-clipboard-history.desc: Android keeps only the last thing you copied. Here is where to find recent clips in your keyboard, and how to keep a searchable history that does not disappear.
android-clipboard-history.intro: Android itself remembers only the last thing you copied — copy something new and the previous text is gone. If you want to get back an address, a code or a sentence you copied earlier, you need a place that keeps a history. There are two: your keyboard, and a clipboard manager app.

sections.h: Option 1: the clipboard in your keyboard
p: Many keyboards have their own clipboard. In Gboard, tap the clipboard icon in the toolbar above the keys (turn it on the first time). Samsung Keyboard has a clipboard button in its toolbar too.

This is the quickest way to grab something you copied a few minutes ago. The catch is that keyboard clipboards are short-term: Gboard, for example, removes unpinned items after about an hour, and you only see the list while you are typing.

sections.h: Option 2: a clipboard manager that keeps a real history
p: If you copy the same things again and again — addresses, account numbers, canned replies — a clipboard manager keeps them until you delete them, lets you search them, and can show them over any app.
Clipboard+ (our app) keeps the text and images you copy in a history, newest first, with search and a floating panel you can open over the app you are using.
steps: Install Clipboard+ from Google Play and open it once.
Copy text as usual. You can also select text in any app and choose Clipboard+ in the selection menu to save it.
Open the floating panel (or the app) to see your history, tap a clip to copy it again, and paste it where you are.
Keep things you reuse as snippets in groups, so they are always one tap away.

p: For a one-off — pasting something you copied a minute ago — the keyboard clipboard is enough. If you lose clips you wanted, or you keep retyping the same text, a clipboard manager saves that time. Clipboard+ is free to start; Pro adds sync with the Windows app through your own Google Drive, unlimited image clips and PDF export.

faq.q: Does Android have a built-in clipboard history?
faq.a: Not in the system itself — Android keeps only the latest clip. Keyboards such as Gboard and Samsung Keyboard add a short-term clipboard list.

faq.q: Can I see clipboard history from my phone on my PC?
faq.a: Yes, with Clipboard+ on both: the Android app and Clipboard+ for Windows sync through your own Google Drive (a Pro feature on Android).

open-app-automatically-after-reboot-andr.title: How to open an app automatically after a reboot on Android (no root)
open-app-automatically-after-reboot-andr.desc: Android has no setting that launches an app when the phone starts. Here is how to make your apps open by themselves after a restart, without root — and how to test it without rebooting.
open-app-automatically-after-reboot-andr.intro: Android does not have a setting that opens an app when the phone starts. If you open the same apps after every restart — a navigation app in the car, a launcher on a kiosk tablet, a music app on a head unit — an auto-start app can do it for you.

sections.h: Why it doesn't happen on its own
p: Since Android 10, apps are not allowed to open screens from the background on their own. An app that should open others after a reboot therefore needs the "Display over other apps" permission, and it can only start them once the phone has been unlocked for the first time.
AutoStart+ (our app) opens the apps you pick after every restart, as soon as you unlock the phone. It needs no root.
steps: Install AutoStart+ from Google Play and open it.
Tap Add apps and choose the apps you want to open after a reboot. Drag the rows to set which one opens first.
Allow "Display over other apps" when asked — without it Android blocks the launch.
Tap Test it now to see what will happen, without restarting the phone.
Restart the phone and unlock it: your apps open in the order you set.

sections.h: Car head units and devices that sleep
p: Many Android head units don't really reboot — they go to sleep when the car is off. AutoStart+ has a Car Mode that opens your apps again every time the screen wakes up.

faq.q: Do I need root to auto start apps on Android?
faq.a: No. AutoStart+ works without root; it only needs the "Display over other apps" permission.

faq.q: Why don't my apps open before I unlock the phone?
faq.a: Android does not let apps open others until the phone has been unlocked once after a reboot. Your apps open right after you unlock.

faq.q: How many apps can I auto start for free?
faq.a: The free version starts 1 app per boot. Pro starts your whole list in order, and a short ad unlocks the limit for 24 hours if you'd rather not subscribe.

floating-notes-over-other-apps-android.title: How to keep a note on top of other apps on Android
floating-notes-over-other-apps-android.desc: Keep a note visible while you use another app: a floating note that stays over any app, folds into a small chip, and can pop up at a time you choose.
floating-notes-over-other-apps-android.intro: Copying a list into a form, checking a recipe while a video plays, keeping an order number in view in a chat — switching back and forth to your notes app breaks the flow. A floating note stays on screen over whatever app you are using.

p: A floating note is a small window drawn over other apps. Android allows this through the "Display over other apps" permission, which you grant once. The note stays on top while you keep using the app underneath.
FloatNote+ (our app) floats each note as a small chip over any app. Tap the chip and it opens as a card right there; tap its title bar to fold it back.
steps: Install FloatNote+ from Google Play and allow "Display over other apps".
Tap + to write a note — it appears over your screen as a card.
Open the app you need. The note stays on top; fold it into a chip when you want the screen back.
Use colors, bold, text size and pictures to make notes easy to tell apart.
To bring a note up at a set time, open its ⋮ menu and choose Remind me — once, every day, weekdays or the days you pick.

p: FloatNote+ for Windows floats the same kind of notes over any window, and the two apps sync through your own Google Drive (a Pro feature on Android).

faq.q: Does Android have floating notes built in?
faq.a: Android has no general floating-note feature. Apps like FloatNote+ add it using the "Display over other apps" permission.

faq.q: Can a note pop up at a set time?
faq.a: Yes. In FloatNote+, set a reminder from the note's ⋮ menu and the note comes up on screen with a notification. The free version keeps one reminder; Pro has no limit.

faq.q: Is FloatNote+ free?
faq.a: Saving notes is free and unlimited, and the free version floats one note at a time. Pro adds unlimited floating notes, inline images, adjustable opacity, Google Drive sync and no ads.

floating-timer-over-other-apps-android.title: How to keep a timer on screen while using other apps on Android
floating-timer-over-other-apps-android.desc: The Clock app's timer disappears when you switch apps. Here is how to keep a countdown, stopwatch or counter floating over any app.
floating-timer-over-other-apps-android.intro: The timer in the Clock app runs in the background, but you can't see it while you are in another app — you have to pull down notifications or switch back. For studying with a lecture, timing a presentation, or a game, it helps to have the time on screen the whole time.

p: FloatTimer+ (our app) floats timers, stopwatches and tally counters over any app as small cards you can drag anywhere.
steps: Install FloatTimer+ from Google Play and allow "Display over other apps".
Create a timer — any hours, minutes and seconds, or a quick preset such as 25 minutes.
Float it and open the app you are using. Start, pause and reset from the card itself.
Fold it into a bubble when you need the space; the time keeps running.

sections.h: More than one at a time
p: You can make as many timers, counters and stopwatches as you like for free, and they keep running. The free version shows one on screen at a time; Pro floats as many as you want at once, or a short ad unlocks that for 24 hours.

faq.q: Can I see a timer over YouTube or a game?
faq.a: Yes. A floating timer stays on top of any app, including videos and games, once you allow "Display over other apps".

faq.q: Is there a Pomodoro preset?
faq.a: FloatTimer+ has 1, 5, 10, 25, 30 and 60-minute quick presets, so a 25-minute focus timer is one tap.

hide-personal-info-in-screenshots.title: How to hide personal info in a screenshot before you share it
hide-personal-info-in-screenshots.desc: Blur, a light pen or a highlighter can leave text readable. Here is how to cover phone numbers, card numbers and faces so they can't be recovered — on your phone, without uploading anything.
hide-personal-info-in-screenshots.intro: Screenshots and photos of documents often carry more than you meant to share: a phone number, an ID or card number, an address, a face, a QR code. Before posting or sending them, cover that information properly.

p: A semi-transparent highlighter or thin pen strokes can leave text readable once someone raises the contrast, and blur or mosaic on small text can sometimes be guessed. Use a solid, opaque box over anything private, and share a copy rather than the original.
Most gallery apps have a markup or drawing tool. If you use it, pick a solid shape or a fully opaque pen, cover each item completely, and zoom in to check the edges before you save.

PhotoCleaner+ (our app) is made for this job. It suggests likely personal information, you review each box, and it exports a copy with solid masks — everything runs on your phone, nothing is uploaded.
steps: Open a photo, screenshot or PDF in PhotoCleaner+.
Check the suggested boxes — phone numbers, emails, card numbers and similar text — and add your own by drawing.
Move, resize or delete boxes until everything private is covered.
Export the masked copy and share that. Your original is not changed, and saved copies carry no EXIF or GPS data.

faq.q: Is blurring enough to hide a phone number?
faq.a: Not always. Light blur on small text can sometimes be read or guessed. A solid, opaque mask is the safe choice.

faq.q: Does PhotoCleaner+ upload my photos?
faq.a: No. Detection and masking run on your phone, and your photos and documents are never uploaded.

faq.q: Is it free?
faq.a: Detection, editing and masking are free; you can export 3 times a day. Pro removes the daily limit and adds PDF export and printing, or a short ad lifts the limit for 24 hours.

sticky-notes-always-on-top-windows.title: How to keep a sticky note always on top on Windows
sticky-notes-always-on-top-windows.desc: Notes on the desktop end up behind the window you are working in. Here is how to pin a note on top of every window — with PowerToys, or with notes that float by design.
sticky-notes-always-on-top-windows.intro: A sticky note is only useful if you can see it. On Windows, notes on the desktop usually end up behind the browser, document or spreadsheet you are working in, so you have to dig for them. There are two ways to keep a note on top.

sections.h: Option 1: pin a window with PowerToys
p: Microsoft PowerToys, a free set of utilities from Microsoft, includes Always On Top. Install PowerToys, turn on Always On Top, click the window you want to keep in front — for example a notes window — and press Win+Ctrl+T. Press it again to unpin.
This works for almost any window. The catch is that a pinned window is a full window: it takes focus when you click it, and it covers the same space whether you are reading the note or not.

sections.h: Option 2: notes that float by design
p: FloatNote+ for Windows (our app) keeps each note as a small chip above every window. Click the chip and it opens as a card right there; press Esc and it folds back. Chips never take focus from the app behind them, so your cursor stays where you were typing.
steps: Install FloatNote+ from the Microsoft Store.
Create a note from the tray icon or with a global hotkey — it appears as a card over your screen.
Keep working: the note stays above every window. Press Esc to fold it into a chip.
Drag chips anywhere, use colors and rich text to tell them apart, and set a reminder to bring a note up at a set time.

sections.h: Your notes on your phone too
p: FloatNote+ for Windows syncs with the FloatNote+ Android app through your own Google Drive, so a note you write on your PC is on your phone. Every feature of the Windows version is free.

faq.q: Can Windows Sticky Notes stay on top of other windows?
faq.a: Not by themselves in most setups. You can pin any window, including a notes window, with PowerToys Always On Top (Win+Ctrl+T), or use an app whose notes float above other windows by design.

faq.q: Does a floating note steal focus from what I'm typing?
faq.a: FloatNote+ chips don't. Clicking or dragging a chip leaves your cursor in the app you were using; only an opened card takes focus, because you type into it.

clipboard-history-windows.title: How to see your clipboard history on Windows
clipboard-history-windows.desc: Windows has a built-in clipboard history (Win+V), but it is short and is cleared when you restart. Here is how to use it, and how to keep a searchable history that lasts.
clipboard-history-windows.intro: Copy something new and the previous clip is gone — unless you keep a history. Windows 10 and 11 have one built in, and a clipboard manager can keep a longer one.

p: Press Win+V. The first time, Windows asks you to turn clipboard history on (you can also do it in Settings > System > Clipboard). After that, Win+V shows your recent clips, and clicking one pastes it.
It is quick, but limited: it keeps up to 25 items, and everything except pinned items is cleared when you restart the PC. There is no search, and it does not reach your phone.

sections.h: Option 2: a clipboard manager that keeps everything
p: Clipboard+ for Windows (our app) sits in the tray and saves the text and images you copy the moment you copy them. Your history stays until you delete it, and you can search it, organize it into groups and snippets, and pull it up with a hotkey.
steps: Install Clipboard+ from the Microsoft Store; it starts in the system tray.
Copy as usual — every text and image clip is saved automatically.
Press the global hotkey to open the quick-pick popup at your cursor, pick a clip with Ctrl+1–9 and press Enter to paste it.
Open the window to search, pin, edit, or keep frequently used text as snippets.

p: Paired with the Clipboard+ Android app, what you copy on your phone pastes on your PC and the other way around, through your own Google Drive. Clipboard history, snippets, groups, search and the quick-pick popup are free; Pro adds sync, unlimited image storage and PDF export.

faq.q: Why is my Win+V clipboard history empty after a restart?
faq.a: Windows clears clipboard history when the PC restarts, except for pinned items. A clipboard manager such as Clipboard+ keeps your history across restarts.

faq.q: How many items does Windows clipboard history keep?
faq.a: Up to 25. Older items drop off as you copy new ones.

timer-always-on-top-windows.title: How to keep a timer on top of other windows on Windows
timer-always-on-top-windows.desc: Keep a countdown visible while you work in other windows — with the Clock app's "Keep on top", or with timers that float as small cards over everything.
timer-always-on-top-windows.intro: Timing a presentation, a focus session or a call is easier when the time stays in view. Windows offers one built-in way, and a floating-timer app adds more.

sections.h: Option 1: "Keep on top" in the Clock app
p: The Clock app that comes with Windows can show a timer in a small window that stays above other windows: start a timer, expand it, and choose Keep on top. It works for a single timer and shows it in a fixed small window.
FloatTimer+ for Windows (our app) floats timers, counters and stopwatches above every window as small pastel cards. Cards never take focus, so clicking one leaves your cursor where you were typing.
steps: Install FloatTimer+ from the Microsoft Store; it lives in the system tray.
Create a timer, counter or stopwatch and float it.
Start, pause and reset from the card itself; drag it anywhere or resize it.
Collapse it into a small bubble, or push it against the screen edge, when you want the space back.

p: You can make as many timers, counters and stopwatches as you like, with no ads. The free version floats one card at a time; Pro is a one-time purchase that floats as many as you want and adds repeating timers and custom alerts.

faq.q: Does Windows have an always-on-top timer?
faq.a: The Clock app's Keep on top shows one timer in a small window above others. For several timers, counters or stopwatches at once, use a floating-timer app.

faq.q: Will a floating timer get in the way of my work?
faq.a: FloatTimer+ cards never take focus from the app underneath, and you can collapse them into a bubble or tuck them against the screen edge.

reading-ruler-dyslexia-adhd-android.title: Reading ruler for dyslexia and ADHD on Android: keep your place while reading
reading-ruler-dyslexia-adhd-android.desc: Losing the line, skipping rows or re-reading the same sentence? A reading ruler or reading mask over any app helps your eyes stay on track. Here is how to set one up on Android.
reading-ruler-dyslexia-adhd-android.intro: Long text on a phone screen is easy to get lost in: your eyes slip to the next line, skip a row, or come back to a sentence you already read. Many people with dyslexia or ADHD use a ruler or a card under the line when reading on paper. On a phone, a reading ruler does the same job on screen.

p: Android's accessibility and display settings — larger font size, bold text, dark theme — can make text easier to read. They don't, however, mark the line you are on, which is what helps when your eyes keep wandering.

sections.h: Add a reading ruler with ReadFocus+
p: ReadFocus+ (our app) floats a focus strip on top of any app — ebooks, PDFs, browsers, news, webtoons. Choose Line Highlight to light up the line you are reading, or Reading Mask to dim everything except your reading zone.
steps: Install ReadFocus+ from Google Play and allow "Display over other apps".
Pick a mode: Line Highlight (a reading ruler) or Reading Mask.
Open the app you're reading in and drag the strip to your line.
Adjust its height (50–300 dp), opacity and color theme until it feels comfortable.

p: The free version gives 60 minutes of overlay time per session and 3 color themes. Pro removes ads and the time limit and adds all 10 themes and keep-screen-on, or a short ad unlocks Pro features for 24 hours.

faq.q: Does a reading ruler help with dyslexia?
faq.a: Many readers with dyslexia or ADHD find that marking the current line makes it easier to keep their place. It is a reading aid, not a treatment — try it and keep the settings that feel comfortable.

faq.q: Which apps does ReadFocus+ work with?
faq.a: Any app on screen: ebook and PDF readers, browsers, news, study notes, comics and webtoons.

reading-ruler-windows.title: How to use a reading ruler on Windows (for dyslexia and ADHD)
reading-ruler-windows.desc: Edge's Immersive Reader has Line focus for web pages. For PDFs, documents and every other app, a click-through focus strip keeps your eyes on the line. Here is how to use both.
reading-ruler-windows.intro: Reading long pages on a monitor makes it easy to lose the line. A reading ruler highlights the line you are on, or dims the rest of the screen, so your eyes stay on track.

sections.h: Option 1: Line focus in Microsoft Edge
p: Microsoft Edge has Immersive Reader, a clean reading view for web pages. In its reading preferences, Line focus highlights one, three or five lines at a time. It only works on pages that open in Immersive Reader, not in PDFs, documents or other apps.

sections.h: Option 2: a focus strip over any app
p: ReadFocus+ for Windows (our app) lays a focus strip over whatever you are reading — a web page, a PDF, a document, code. Mask dims the top and bottom of the screen and leaves a clear band; Highlight marks the line you are on. The strip is click-through, so you keep scrolling and clicking underneath as before.
steps: Install ReadFocus+ from the Microsoft Store.
Start it from the floating panel or with a keyboard shortcut, and choose Mask or Highlight.
Move the strip to your line, or nudge it up and down with shortcuts as you read.
Lock it, hide it, or move it to another monitor from the panel.

p: The free version includes both modes and three themes, in sessions of up to 60 minutes. Pro is a one-time purchase that removes the time limit and adds premium themes, strip height and opacity settings, and keep-screen-on. There are no ads.

faq.q: Does Windows have a reading ruler?
faq.a: Edge's Immersive Reader has Line focus for web pages. For other apps — PDFs, Word, code editors — you need a screen overlay such as ReadFocus+ for Windows.

faq.q: Will the strip block my clicks?
faq.a: No. ReadFocus+ for Windows is click-through: scrolling, selecting and clicking go to the app underneath.

floating-calculator-over-other-apps-andr.title: How to use a calculator on top of other apps on Android
floating-calculator-over-other-apps-andr.desc: Work out a discount or convert a price without leaving your shopping, banking or browser screen: a floating calculator that stays over any app, with unit and currency converters.
floating-calculator-over-other-apps-andr.intro: Checking a price in a shopping app, splitting a bill in a chat, converting a currency while booking — switching to the Calculator app and back means losing your place and remembering numbers in your head. A floating calculator stays on screen over the app you are using.

p: Android can show two apps at once in split screen. Open the recent apps screen, choose split screen for one app and pick the Calculator for the other half. It works, but each app gets only half of the screen.

FloatCalc+ (our app) is a calculator window that floats over any app. The calculator, unit converter and currency converter share one window you can drag anywhere; fold the keypad to a single line or shrink the panel to an icon at the screen edge when you need the space.
steps: Install FloatCalc+ from Google Play and allow "Display over other apps".
Open the floating calculator and drag it where it doesn't cover what you need.
Type the expression — powers, roots and percentages work too — and copy the answer to the clipboard.

faq.a: Yes. A floating calculator such as FloatCalc+ stays on top of other apps once you allow "Display over other apps".

crypto-price-ticker-over-other-apps-andr.intro: Exchange apps show prices inside the app or in a home-screen widget, so checking the market means leaving whatever you are doing. A floating ticker keeps the prices you follow on screen over any app.

make-android-phone-louder.title: How to make your Android phone louder
make-android-phone-louder.desc: Phone too quiet even at full volume? Check these settings first, then see how a volume booster raises the output safely — with the boost shown in decibels.
make-android-phone-louder.intro: If videos, calls on speaker or music are too quiet even at full volume, start with a few settings — sometimes the phone is simply limiting itself. If that isn't enough, a volume booster can raise the output further.

p: Make sure you are turning up the media volume, not the ringtone: press a volume button while a video is playing, or open the volume panel and raise the media slider.

Some phones have a media volume limit. On Samsung phones, look for Media volume limiter in the volume settings. Also try the phone's own sound effects or equalizer if it has one, and check whether a case is covering the speaker.

VolumeBooster+ (our app) raises the system output rather than one app's volume, so videos, music and games get louder. The boost is shown in decibels with Safe, Caution and Danger zones, so you can see how far you have pushed it.
steps: Install VolumeBooster+ from Google Play.
Play something, then raise the boost a little at a time and watch the dB zone.
Use the equalizer presets, bass booster or AutoEQ for your headphones to make it clearer, not just louder.
Turn the boost down when you don't need it — your ears and speaker will thank you.

sections.h: Free and Pro, and your hearing
p: Free boosts up to +10 dB for 60 minutes a day; Pro or a 24-hour Free Pass opens the full +15 dB range. The dB value is an estimate, and the app is not a medical device — if you notice ear pain or ringing, lower the volume.

faq.q: Can a volume booster damage my speaker or hearing?
faq.a: Very high volume can. Raise the boost gradually, keep an eye on the Safe/Caution/Danger zones, and lower it if sound distorts or your ears hurt.

faq.q: How much louder can it go?
faq.a: Up to +15 dB with Pro or a Free Pass, and up to +10 dB on the free version. Actual loudness varies by device, headphones and content.

hide-personal-info-in-screenshots-window.title: How to hide personal info in screenshots and PDFs on Windows

hide-personal-info-in-screenshots-window.intro: Screenshots and scanned documents often contain a phone number, an email, a card or ID number, an address or a face. Before you send or post them from your PC, cover that information so it can't be recovered.

p: Recent versions of Snipping Tool on Windows 11 can hide email addresses and phone numbers in a screenshot through Text actions, and you can draw over anything else. Avoid the highlighter for this — it is semi-transparent — and use solid strokes that cover each item completely.

Review the boxes: click to turn one on or off, drag to move or resize, and draw your own over anything that was missed.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded?

crypto-price-ticker-on-top-windows.desc: Watch the coins you follow while you work: a slim price ticker above every window, price alerts as desktop notifications, and charts on a double-click.
